source_evidence: A firm’s relationship summary tells you about: the types of services a firm offers; the fees and costs you will have to pay for those services; conflicts of interest a broker or adviser may have;
answer: A client relationship summary, also called Form CRS, is a disclosure that registered broker-dealers and registered investment advisers must provide to retail investors. It describes the firm’s services, fees and costs, potential conflicts of interest, the standard of conduct associated with its services, and whether the firm or its professionals have reportable legal or disciplinary history. It also includes questions you can use to start a conversation with a financial professional. Similar headings and topic order make summaries easier to compare across firms.
